learning.why: The teacher explicitly wrote both 3+7=10 on the board and asked the reverse, hinting they are the same; child saw that pattern.
Child is now considering that maybe 3 and 7 also work, since teacher showed it, but isn't fully letting go yet.

end.summary:
Practised finding number partners that make 10.
Answered 5 of 6 partner questions without help.
Listed 2 of 3 different pairs without help.
Recognised that 3+7 and 7+3 both make 10.
The idea that only 5+5 makes 10 was corrected later with examples including 2+8 and 9+1; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Gauri practised making 10 with fingers, beads, and number pairs. They used the “how many are left?” method and correctly found several partners, including 2 with 8, 9 with 1, and 3 with 7 in either order. They first thought only 5+5 made 10, but this was corrected later using more examples. At home, ask Gauri to find three different pairs that make 10, then switch the order of each pair.
